name: Banner
summary: Page-level system state strip. Stretches edge-to-edge, sticks above the page header, communicates state that affects the entire app — maintenance windows, outages, trial countdowns, account suspension, environment indicators (sandbox / test mode). Distinct from Alert (region-scoped) and Toast (transient).

tone.description: promo: branded marketing-launch lane (uses the v0.11 spring-green accent strip with brand voice text). sandbox: pinstripe lime/canvas pattern indicating non-production environment.

action.description: Optional inline action — typically a Link, sometimes a small Button. 'Upgrade now', 'Restore service', 'Switch to production'.

dismissible.description: Sandbox + danger banners are generally non-dismissible. Promo + info banners are dismissible with a remember-me cookie.

sticky.description: When true, position:sticky above the Navbar. False renders inline at the document top.

compact.description: Single-line layout, smaller type. The default is compact; multi-line banners need a Modal instead.

keyboard: Tab - move focus to inline action
Tab - move focus to dismiss button
rules: danger banners additionally set role='alert' so SR announces them immediately on appearance.
Sandbox / test-mode banners stay non-dismissible — users in non-production envs need the persistent reminder.
Glyph + label + color — never color alone.
Promo banner copy follows ADR 0018 brand voice — sentence case, ≤ 12 words.

do: Reserve Banner for state that affects the whole app or environment.
Render sandbox / test-mode banners with a pinstripe pattern so SR users hear 'Sandbox' AND sighted users see a non-uniform fill.
Pair every banner with an action when the user can act on the state ('Upgrade', 'Reconnect').
Stack at most one Banner at a time. If you have two, design the most important and route the second to an inbox.
Sticky position above the Navbar — the user must not lose context.
dont: Don't use Banner for region-scoped messages. Use Alert.
Don't use Banner for transient confirmation. Use Toast.
Don't render Banner as a marketing teaser. The promo tone is for actual launch / pricing / GA announcements, not 'check out our new blog post'.
Don't make a danger Banner dismissible.
Don't paint a sandbox banner in solid lime — the action accent stays for actions. Pinstripe / faint canvas-tinted fill instead.

changelog.note: Initial Banner contract. Six tones including sandbox + promo. Sticky-by-default. Pinstripe sandbox fill so the env indicator never disappears.
